title: S2: execution waves in daemon.dispatch behind [scheduler].mode = shadow|active|off — interference-compatible wave logged to runs/sched/waves.jsonl, applied only in active mode
spec:
Goal T-0503, brief .orchestrator/adaptive-parallelism-program.md section P3 (select the best set of mutually compatible ready tasks; respect depends_on, capacity, budgets, cooldowns, safety policy) and Evaluation (retain what baseline scheduling would have done). Base goal/T-0503 with S0a (schedlog, dispatch.jsonl considered rows, first_ready_at) and S1 (interference.select_wave) merged. Work only in your worktree, commit only on your own branch with the task id in the message, run the full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh before reporting; report sha and failures only.
Facts: daemon.dispatch walks queued execute tasks in id order and dispatches first-come until free_slots (daemon.py free_slots); _load_review_cfg(pool) (daemon.py:217) shows how a pool.toml table is read into module globals with defaults; interference.select_wave(ready, running, tasks, capacity, order=None, graph=None, rules=None) -> {wave, deferred}.
1. _load_scheduler_cfg(pool): table [scheduler] with defaults mode = "shadow" (off|shadow|active), soft_conflict_policy = "defer", max_wave = 0 (0 = capacity). Add the table to .orchestrator/pool.toml with comments (default shadow: dispatch unchanged, waves only logged; active dispatches the wave; off disables both) and to install.py's scaffold only if pool.toml is templated there (check; otherwise leave install.py alone).
2. In dispatch, once per tick: candidates = ready, non-stale queued execute tasks that would dispatch this tick (spec approved or below SPEC_REVIEW_MIN, fallback tier available), in the existing order; running = execute tasks with status running plus dispatched-but-unclaimed ones; order = _wave_order(candidate_ids, tasks), a module-level hook that returns its input unchanged (a later task replaces it with critical-path ranking); result = interference.select_wave(candidate_ids, running_ids, tasks, capacity=min(slots, max_wave or slots), order=order, rules={soft_conflict_policy}). When mode != off and candidates exist, schedlog.append("waves", {"ts","mode","ready": candidate_ids,"running": running_ids,"baseline_order": the first-come ids that would dispatch within slots,"wave": result["wave"],"deferred": result["deferred"],"predicted": interference.pairwise of the wave tasks,"priority": {},"applied": mode == "active"}).
3. mode off or shadow: dispatch exactly as before (first-come). mode active: dispatch the wave in wave order and no other task this tick; each deferred candidate is recorded in the dispatch.jsonl considered row as skipped with reason "predicted_interference" (hard or soft deferral) or "executor_capacity" (capacity deferral). Invariants in every mode: never more dispatches than slots, never a task whose dependencies are not merged, never a hard-conflicting pair co-dispatched in active mode; spec-review creation and the review respawn loop are unchanged.
4. README Pipeline section: one paragraph on [scheduler] modes and the waves log.
5. Tests tests/test_daemon.py: test_scheduler_cfg_defaults, test_dispatch_shadow_logs_wave_and_keeps_first_come, test_dispatch_active_defers_hard_conflict_with_running_task, test_dispatch_active_respects_slots_and_dependencies, test_dispatch_mode_off_writes_no_wave_rows. Existing tests stay green.
acceptance: [scheduler] mode defaults to shadow: dispatch order and set are unchanged and every tick with candidates appends a waves.jsonl row with ready, running, baseline_order, wave, deferred, predicted and applied false

mode active dispatches only the selected wave, never a hard-conflicting pair together, never beyond free slots or unmet dependencies, and records deferred candidates in dispatch.jsonl as predicted_interference or executor_capacity
mode off writes no waves rows and dispatches as before; spec-review creation and review respawn are untouched

tests test_scheduler_cfg_defaults, test_dispatch_shadow_logs_wave_and_keeps_first_come, test_dispatch_active_defers_hard_conflict_with_running_task, test_dispatch_active_respects_slots_and_dependencies, test_dispatch_mode_off_writes_no_wave_rows pass and the full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

constraints.interface_contract: _wave_order(candidate_ids, tasks) module hook returning an ordered id list (S3 replaces it); waves.jsonl row {ts, mode, ready, running, baseline_order, wave, deferred, predicted, priority, applied}; [scheduler] keys mode, soft_conflict_policy, max_wave

result.summary: superseded by S2 v2 after spec review T-0523 request_changes (config loader call site, budget-held retries in the candidate set, id-to-task mapping before pairwise); no code was written

spec_review_risks.issue: _load_review_cfg(pool) (cited in Facts as the pattern to mirror) is only called from tick() (daemon.py:1253), never from dispatch() itself. Every existing Daemon test in tests/test_daemon.py calls daemon.dispatch(pool) directly, never tick(). If _load_scheduler_cfg(pool) mirrors that same tick()-only call site, the five new acceptance tests (which per the established test idiom will call daemon.dispatch(pool) directly, e.g. via the dispatch_telemetry() helper at test_daemon.py:82) can never observe a pool.toml [scheduler] mode of 'active' or 'off' unless they also call _load_scheduler_cfg(pool) first -- something the spec never mentions and no existing test does for _load_review_cfg. This will either make the acceptance tests unwritable as scoped or force an undocumented extra step.

Spec step 2 defines candidates as 'ready, non-stale queued execute tasks that would dispatch this tick,' but the existing dispatch() loop iterates over bus.read(status='queued', role='execute') + retry_held (daemon.py:603-605), where retry_held are budget-held tasks eligible for immediate re-dispatch. The spec never says whether these budget-retry tasks are included in the wave-selection candidate/order set or bypass interference selection entirely. Left ambiguous, an executor could either drop budget-retries from active-mode scheduling (silently changing existing retry behavior) or crash/mishandle them since retry_held tasks have status='held', not 'queued', and the candidate definition says 'queued'.

select_wave's returned wave/deferred/candidate_ids are plain task-id strings, but interference.pairwise(tasks_list, **kwargs) expects an iterable of task mappings (it calls _task_id/_scope on each item directly). Spec step 2's 'predicted: interference.pairwise of the wave tasks' does not say the wave ids must first be resolved back to task dicts (e.g. via the same tasks lookup already built for select_wave) before calling pairwise, which is an easy point to get wrong.
